change: Protocol version 1.0.0 frozen before revised discovery or external expression outcomes.

Specified UniProt reference proteome UP000059680 for the frozen "Oryza reference" mapping. The taxonomy-wide query mixed redundant subspecies/strain proteins and produced only one eligible pathway; the official japonica reference produced 20 under unchanged RBH, coverage, and size gates. Both projections are retained.

Frozen uniform mapping-QC implementation before opening expression outcomes: GenMap 100-mers allowing two mismatches; a gene passes sequence mappability when at least 80% of at least 100 scored union-exon bases have score 1, and passes unique-model QC only when its exons do not overlap another annotated gene. Also froze pathway score/output and expression-plus-exon-length matched-random-set implementation in analysis/config/operational_qc.yaml. No discovery expression outcomes had been opened.

Completed the internal pathway robustness decision rule before opening expression outcomes: camera and roast q<0.10 with primary-direction agreement, primary fgsea q<0.10 after deleting the largest absolute-statistic leading-edge gene, and observed absolute mean signed-Wald score at or above the 95th percentile of 1,000 expression-and-exon-length matched sets. No discovery expression outcomes had been opened.

Completed the conditional DTU gate/filter before expression outcomes: every member of an exact transcript-sequence duplicate cluster is excluded; gene and transcript counts must each be >=10 in >=3 libraries, transcript proportion >=0.05 in >=3 libraries, and >=2 transcripts per gene must remain. The dataset-level gate still requires >=1,000 such genes, >=60% Salmon mapping in every included library, and 30 bootstraps. DRIMSeq/stageR OFDR<0.05 is primary and DEXSeq is sensitivity only.

Frozen the leading-locus observed mapping-bias flag before expression outcomes: require >=100 candidate-overlapping alignments per cultivar; severe cultivar bias requires an absolute mismatch-rate difference >=0.02, >=2-fold mismatch-rate ratio, and >=0.20 lower mean exonic breadth in the higher-mismatch cultivar. Bilateral multi-alignment fractions >0.20 are a separate severe ambiguity failure. Lower coverage is reported as indeterminate for the observed sensitivity but is not itself a failure because uniform combined-reference mappability remains evaluable.

Frozen external factor references, sign standardization, frozen-family multiplicity, signature scoring, pathway tests, and deterministic outcome labels in analysis/config/external_validation.yaml before any external expression outcome was downloaded or opened. PRJNA450886 is cross-context rather than direct replication; PRJNA922966 is generic transfer; PRJNA1090613 remains exploratory only.

Added a fail-closed not_testable branch when frozen discovery pathways exist but none meets the unchanged external mapped-size gate. This prevents an empty enrichment call and does not change thresholds, pathway membership, directions, or decision rules. No external expression outcome had been downloaded or opened.

Frozen targeted annotation, design-matched small-RNA, promoter motif, published-evidence, and deterministic tier implementation rules in analysis/config/orthogonal_validation.yaml before discovery or external expression outcomes were produced. The GEO audit found 12 design-cell matches but zero shared BioSample accessions, so miRNA integration is restricted to condition-level coherence.

Specified external motif transport before any external expression outcome was downloaded or opened: independently select PRJNA450886 primary-24h response genes at genome-wide q<0.05 and |log2FC|>=log2(1.5), test only discovery ROBUST_CANDIDATE_MOTIF PWMs against the same 100 expression/GC-matched backgrounds in both windows, require q<0.05 and OR>=1.5 in >=80 backgrounds per window, and prohibit STREME or replacement response sets externally.

External STAR alignments retain unchanged two-pass mapping, reference, filters, gene counts, featureCounts, and QC metrics but write transient unsorted mapped-read BAMs without coordinate indexes; featureCounts consumes unsorted BAM directly and samtools idxstats scans it. This changes only transient BAM representation, reduces sorting time and peak memory, and was frozen before discovery completion or any external expression outcome access.

Salmon v2.5.1 emits the 96 gentrome decoy contigs as zero-count rows in quant.sf despite correctly flagging them as decoys. Discovery and external DTU loaders now audit these rows in salmon_nontranscript_targets.tsv and exclude targets absent from the frozen transcript-to-gene map before inference. Gene-level tximport already applied the same frozen map. No thresholds, transcript membership definitions, or expression outcomes were changed or viewed.

The cleanup implementation now follows the preregistered 200-GB strategy by removing compressed raw FASTQs together with trimmed reads and eligible BAMs after matrix, QC, and completion manifests verify. Every raw FASTQ is size-checked and its ENA MD5 is recomputed against the retained download-audit row immediately before deletion; counts and bytes are recorded, while download reports and manifests remain retained. No expression outcomes were viewed.

After an abrupt host crash with no kernel OOM record, validated GW_P1/GW_P2 BAMs showed that eight-thread STAR completed successfully but used about 10.6 GB RSS on the 15-GB host. Subsequent discovery and external STAR jobs retain one-alignment concurrency and eight threads while lowering only the BAM sort-RAM ceiling from 6 GB to 4 GB. References, two-pass mapping, filters, gene counts, BAM content semantics, and all statistical rules are unchanged; no discovery inferential or external expression outcomes were viewed.

Live GW_P3 resource measurements under the amended 4-GB sort ceiling showed that STAR's fixed genome-index allocation dominated memory while eight mapping threads used only half of the 16 logical CPUs. For samples started after GW_P3, STAR therefore uses 12 threads, retains single-alignment concurrency, and leaves four CPUs for the operating system. The 4-GB sort ceiling, references, two-pass mapping, filters, gene counts, BAM content semantics, and all statistical rules are unchanged; only mapping throughput is affected, and no discovery inferential or external expression outcomes were viewed.

The post-reboot serial recovery driver incorrectly listed nonexistent accessions SRR18856612, SRR18856611, and SRR18856610 for GW_M1, GW_M2, and GW_M3. Its validated-input gate stopped before any affected alignment began. The driver entries were corrected to SRR18856600, SRR18856599, and SRR18856598, respectively, matching the frozen download audit and biological-unit registry. No expression outcomes or affected alignment outputs were produced under the incorrect mapping.

The discovery DRIMSeq fit completed but stageR stopped because some non-estimable gene and transcript tests had NA p-values. The documented stageR allowNA path is now explicit: genes with NA screening p-values and their transcripts are excluded from stage-wise testing, while NA confirmation p-values remain uncallable; an audit table records both counts. The OFDR threshold, filtering, model, contrast, correction method, and all finite p-values are unchanged. Diagnosis inspected only aggregate NA counts, not gene identities, directions, significance results, or any external outcomes; the external firewall remained closed.

At the resumed discovery run, Snakemake deterministically regenerated the PmiREN-reference and published-evidence audit outputs because their inputs were newer than the retained outputs. Every regenerated manifest entry validates against the unchanged frozen archive, provenance, registry, configuration, and current hashed scripts, but the outer orthogonal bundle still pinned the stale pre-regeneration manifest bytes. Only those two outer manifest hashes are refreshed to the reproducible outputs; evidence inputs, audit contents, gates, thresholds, and decision rules are unchanged, and no external outcome was accessed.

The targeted InterPro Matches implementation incorrectly treated the frozen maximum of 100 sequences per request as a maximum total candidate count and stopped when discovery produced 206 frozen candidate proteins. It now partitions the unchanged complete candidate set deterministically into sequential API requests of at most 100 sequences (100, 100, and 6) and combines the responses before the existing exact-MD5-set validation. No candidate is dropped or reranked; annotation rules, evidence thresholds, and frozen discovery results are unchanged. Discovery result membership was frozen before this correction, and no external expression outcome was accessed.

MEME Suite 5.5.9 AME with the frozen --verbose 1 --text invocation emitted the documented 17 data fields without a header row; the generic TSV reader therefore treated the first result as column names and stopped before interpreting any motif statistics. Discovery and external motif consumers now use the same strict parser that accepts either the official named header or exactly 17 headerless fields in the official order and rejects any other width or malformed row. Motifs, backgrounds, tests, thresholds, multiplicity, and decisions are unchanged; parser fixtures pass for the observed headerless output and the official headered sample, and no external expression outcome was accessed.

After the discovery completion gate passed, the continuation launcher stopped before starting any external study because its host-service PATH provides python3 but no python alias. The two cleanup invocations now use python3, matching the cleanup script shebang and its standard-library-only implementation. Cleanup verification rules, study order, analysis workflows, thresholds, and results are unchanged; no external expression outcome was accessed before this correction.

The first external STAR alignment completed, but samtools 1.24 refused its legacy sequential idxstats fallback because the preregistered low-memory BAM is intentionally unsorted and unindexed. The workflow now derives the same four idxstats columns in a single sequential samtools-view/awk pass, including reference-header order and mapped/unmapped flag semantics. STAR parameters, BAM content, featureCounts, QC gates, contrasts, thresholds, and all validation rules are unchanged. Only first-sample operational QC logs were inspected; no condition comparison, differential-expression, pathway, signature, motif-transport, or validation outcome had been computed or opened.

The exploratory PRJNA1090613 metadata uses SFZ_unresolved, but three external model implementations and their configuration expected SFZ, converting half the samples to NA and making the prespecified cultivar-by-infection design rank-deficient. Replaced only this factor level and corresponding coefficient and contrast names with SFZ_unresolved across gene, pathway, and DTU models. The study remains exploratory only, with the same formula, reference, sign, thresholds, multiplicity, and cannot-promote rules; synthetic gene/pathway and DTU tests plus the production DTU gate passed. Diagnosis used metadata, aggregate QC, and the design failure; no per-gene, pathway, signature, or DTU identity, direction, effect, p value, or q value was viewed before the correction.
